newsitem.title: JAPAN: Victor interim profit up 20% on robust sales.
newsitem.headline: Victor interim profit up 20% on robust sales.

text.p: Audio and video equipment maker Victor Co of Japan Ltd said on Thursday its interim profits rose 20 percent from a year earlier thanks to robust sales and the weaker yen.

Victor said its parent sales rose 4.2 percent year-on-year to 283.4 billion yen ($2.5 billion) for the six months to September 30, leading to a 20.3 percent jump in half-year current profit to 3.0 billion yen ($26.5 million).
Current profit is pretax and includes gains or losses on non-operating activities, such as investment in stocks.
The company also saw an operational profit of 312 million yen ($2.76 million). It has not had any operational profits in five years.
The company said robust sales of its pocket-sized digital video cameras, high-definition televisions and electronic devices contributed to the strong earnings.
The dollar's 13 percent rally to 113 yen from its year-ago level also favoured the interim earnings, it said.

The weaker yen, which in theory boosts yen-denominated exporting income, will likely create an extra profit of 2.4 billion yen ($21.2 million) in the full year ending on March 31, a company official said.
Nevertheless, declines in prices at which its consumer appliances are marketed had been a considerable blow, the official said.
For example, the number of video players sold in the first half year increased six percent from a year earlier, but prices declined by an average of 15 percent.

For the full year to March 31, 1997, the company expects parent sales of 590 billion yen ($5.22 billion), up from 562.5 billion the previous year, and parent current profit of eight billion yen ($70.7 million), up from 5.5 billion yen ($48.6 million) a year earlier. ($1=113 yen)
